_: Settlement sheet for Greenspring (2.5c), from its catalogue record.

norms.text: Water from the spring is given free to any traveller.
Beds and rope are sold at one price that the village agreed together.
A visitor tastes the water before speaking.

taboos.text: Fouling the pool under the Hist.

values.text: Being indispensable to the travellers bound for Helstrom.
Clean water that can be drunk unboiled.

contempts.text: The salt works upstream, which the village blames for the salt in the spring.
Cult couriers, tappers and Veiled Reed factors who use the lodge as an inn.

place.text: The spring is the reason the village stands here; travellers bound for Helstrom have no surer water.

work.text: Water is free, but beds and rope pay for everything else.

people.text: Travellers are fed and housed for a price; most of them are gone by morning.

trade.text: Beds and rope fetch a great deal from travellers bound for Helstrom.

danger.text: Salt is reaching the spring and the Hist has begun to sicken.

rumour.text: Talk at the lodge is of the salt and of who will carry the next load to Helstrom.

directions.text: Helstrom lies south-west past Ux-Aneet; the landing is below the huts.

addressTerms.text: Travellers are called traveller, or by their errand.
The three office-holders are called by office: minder, keeper, herald.

oaths.text: By the root that holds us.

neverSaid.text: That the spring could sour for good.

grievances.text: Salt is reaching the spring from upstream.

rumours.text: Couriers bound for Helstrom carry more than their ledgers declare.

views.text: The Conclave sent the village its tree-minder's office; the village keeps faith with it.

dissent.text: Holds the spring's ladle at the stone lip and will not grant that the spring is souring. She is wrong; the minder and the jar-filler taste the salt.
